item.title: Paper: Explainability Assistant: A Conversational XAI Interface for Interpreting Energy Consumption Models
item.description: This research introduces a conversational interface that helps non-technical users interpret complex energy forecasting models, making machine learning insights more accessible for facility management.

item.title: Paper: ORCH: Organizational Principles Enable Collective Intelligence in Embodied AI
item.description: The authors propose a framework that applies human organizational theory to multi-agent systems, allowing AI collectives to dynamically adapt their structure based on specific task requirements.

item.title: Paper: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
item.description: This paper introduces a benchmark to test whether foundation models can grasp fundamental topological concepts like continuity and enclosure, which are essential for true spatial reasoning.

item.title: Paper: Nuha-Speech: Building General-Purpose Arabic Speech-LLMs
item.description: The authors developed a comprehensive dataset and training pipeline to improve the performance of speech-based large language models specifically for the Arabic language.

item.title: Paper: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents
item.description: The authors introduce procedural graphs to structure LLM agent workflows, preventing common issues like repetitive actions and poor long-term planning in complex task execution.

item.title: Paper: ReCite: Agentic Reasoning for Faithful Citation
item.description: This method improves citation accuracy in LLMs by forcing agents to verify that retrieved documents logically support specific claims, reducing the risk of misleading academic references.

item.title: Paper: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
item.description: The researchers demonstrate that iteratively improving the system environment (harness) allows smaller, cheaper models to achieve high performance on complex enterprise tasks.

item.title: Paper: Distill Globally, Adapt Locally: Reasoning Distillation and Product-Type Test-Time Training for Scalable Trade-Up Recommendation
item.description: This framework efficiently scales product recommendations by distilling complex LLM reasoning into a lightweight model that adapts to specific product categories, saving significant computational costs.

item.title: Paper: Does Your Agent's Memory Survive a Model Upgrade? A Controlled Study of Memory Portability
item.description: This study evaluates how different memory storage methods—like raw history versus knowledge graphs—affect an agent's ability to retain information when the underlying LLM is upgraded.

item.title: Paper: Large Language Models for HVAC Operations in Building Energy Systems: A Critical Review of Methods, Applications, and Deployment Readiness

item.title: Paper: PRICE: A Systematic Study of LLM Adaptation Choices for Bitcoin Price Forecasting
item.description: This research tests various fine-tuning and prompting strategies for using quantized LLMs to predict Bitcoin price movements, providing a roadmap for applying LLMs to volatile financial time-series data.

item.title: Paper: SENTINEL-RL: Offloading Topological Reasoning from LLM Agents in the Security Operations Center
item.description: This architecture improves cybersecurity SOC agents by using graph encoders to handle large network topologies, preventing LLMs from making invalid containment decisions due to context limits.

item.title: Paper: When Models Edit Too Much: On the Fidelity of Minimal Code Edits
item.description: Researchers found that even top-tier LLMs often rewrite more code than necessary when fixing bugs, which complicates code reviews and reduces the maintainability of automated patches.

item.title: Paper: The Dice Roll Method: A Standardized Protocol for Repeated-Query Auditing of Large Language Model Brand Recommendations
item.description: This paper introduces a standardized statistical framework for auditing how consistently LLMs recommend brands, helping practitioners measure and account for model output variance.

item.title: Paper: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models II: One Training Example
item.description: The authors demonstrate that LLMs can learn effective policies from just a single training example through on-policy distillation, challenging assumptions about the necessity of massive datasets.
